findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` to Scope and state how its `judge()` call-count assertion (`len(rec.models) == 4`, line 142) is updated for the batched call shape, deriving the affected-test list from a `find_referencing_symbols`/grep sweep of `judge` rather than by hand.
evidence: Scope enumerates for tests only: `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py — batch payload shape, demultiplexing, and fail-safe tests.`
Approach: `Today judge() issues 2N calls ... Batched, it issues 2 * ceil(N / batch) calls` — the call-count change that invalidates the omitted test's assertion.

tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py:142 `assert len(rec.models) == 4  # two candidates x both orderings` inside `test_overlap_judge_selects_the_standard_class_for_every_pair`, which imports and calls `judge` (lines 131–141).
grep of `judge(` returns hits in `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py` (lines 134, 241) not covered by Scope.
findings.finding: The plan changes the call-count behavior of `judge()` (2N calls become 2*ceil(N/batch)), but its affected-file inventory under Scope lists only `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` as the test file and omits `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`, which structurally references `judge()` and asserts its exact call count. `test_overlap_judge_selects_the_standard_class_for_every_pair` (line 128) calls `judge(...)` with 2 candidates and asserts `len(rec.models) == 4` ("two candidates x both orderings", line 142) — an assertion the batching change directly invalidates. An LSP/grep sweep of `judge` references surfaces this file; the hand-listed Scope misses it.
findings.location: Scope — the bullet `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py — batch payload shape, demultiplexing, and fail-safe tests.` (the only test file enumerated)
scenarios: `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py::test_overlap_judge_selects_the_standard_class_for_every_pair` (line 142) asserts `len(rec.models) == 4` for 2 candidates x both orderings — batching reduces the call count below 4, so this existing test breaks and is not accounted for in Scope, leaving the gate-passing claim (`pytest ... exit 0`) unmet.

`tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py::test_overlap_judge_failure_is_an_abstain_not_a_raise` (line 240) drives `judge()` and must be re-checked under the batched fail-safe path, but the file is absent from the affected-file inventory.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, add a bullet for `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py`: update `test_overlap_judge_selects_the_standard_class_for_every_pair` so its call-count assertion reflects `2*ceil(N/batch)` instead of `2N`, and confirm `test_overlap_judge_failure_is_an_abstain_not_a_raise` still holds under the batched path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the per-candidate label vocabulary (exact token form, e.g. `C1..Cn` or the ticket-id) and add a co-located rule in overlap_judge.md's BATCH section instructing the model to echo that exact label verbatim into `candidate_id`, so the 'matched by label' demux has a defined, unambiguous key.
evidence: Plan Testing: 'a canned batched response maps back to exactly one verdict per candidate, matched by label and not by position; … a response entry naming an unknown label … resolve[s] to abstain'

Plan Scope: contract entries 'each carrying `candidate_id`'; md section describes 'per-candidate independence, and one echoed verdict per candidate' but not a verbatim-echo rule or the label token set

ABSENCE: no definition of what the label token IS, nor an instruction that the model must copy the user-message label into `candidate_id` — without which 'matched by label' has no defined key and every candidate could silently abstain
overlap_judge.md today defines only the single-pair FIRST/SECOND framing; the label-echo contract is new and must be co-located with the `candidate_id` schema field it drives
findings.finding: The batched demux keys on a per-candidate LABEL ('matched by label and not by position'; an 'unknown label' or absent entry abstains), and the new contract entry carries `candidate_id`, but the plan never defines the label VOCABULARY (are labels ticket-ids, or synthetic C1/C2 tags?) nor states the co-located prompt rule that the model must ECHO the exact user-message label verbatim into `candidate_id`. The decision rule that makes label-based demux correct is left unspecified where the schema field it fills lives.
findings.location: Scope → overlap_judge.md / contracts.py bullets; Testing → 'Demultiplexing'; Approach mechanism 2
scenarios: Model echoes a paraphrased or truncated label (e.g. a shortened ticket-id) → no exact match → every candidate abstains despite valid verdicts
Labels are real ticket-ids that also appear in `key_entities` digest text → the model conflates the label with a cited entity, mislabelling verdicts
findings.suggested_fix: Specify a synthetic, collision-free label (e.g. `CANDIDATE 1..N`), state in the md BATCH section 'copy the CANDIDATE label exactly into `candidate_id`', and add a demux test asserting a paraphrased/near-miss label abstains only its own candidate.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile leaf-parent containment: either re-home c403 under a parent whose plan contains overlap-judge token/cache economics (e.g. the overlap-judge epic that owns overlap/judge.py), or enumerate the overlap-judge cost-reduction line (8415 / c403 / e3cd) explicitly in epic 061c's plan so the leaf is a demonstrable subset of its parent's declared scope.
evidence: Leaf parent_id and managed_refs both point to epic 061c, whose declared scope is 'src/rebar/llm/runner.py … providers.py … structured.py … config.py … plan_review/sidecar.py … completion_sidecar.py … parity.py … infra/terraform … docs/llm-framework.md' and whose ACs are all Bedrock/provider-seam/provenance.

Leaf Scope is 'src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py … reviewers/overlap_judge.md … contracts.py (overlap_verdict_batch) … tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py' — none of which appear in the epic's plan, ACs, or file_impact.
overlap/judge.py's own docstring attributes it to a different epic: 'Stage-2 bounded LLM pairwise overlap judge (epic only-crave-art, story 9022)'.

The epic's own parenting comment content-searched only for provider-seam vocabulary ('provider seam, providers.py, bedrock, model class, ProviderSession, ModelProfile, provider_provenance, model_ladder, resolve_model_string, per-pass model') and deliberately excluded unrelated subsystems — confirming overlap-judge cache economics is not the epic's declared line of work.

Mitigation: the leaf is linked discovered_from sibling story 8415 (itself an epic child), which explicitly handed off 'batching several candidates into one call … belongs on its own ticket, filed as discovered work with these measurements attached' — so the work faithfully continues established sibling scope; the gap is that the epic's PLAN does not enumerate that line, not that the work is invented.
findings.finding: The leaf c403's declared parent is the provider-seam epic 061c ('LLM provider seam — Bedrock + OpenAI-compatible, tiered verdict provenance'), but the leaf delivers overlap-judge token/cache economics (batching in overlap/judge.py, a BATCH section in overlap_judge.md, a new overlap_verdict_batch contract, cache-floor measurement) that the epic's plan, ACs, and file-impact do not contain and do not imply. The leaf steps outside the parent's declared scope; it is not a subset of it.
scenarios: An epic-level plan review or completion check reads 061c's scope as the provider seam and finds a child delivering overlap-judge prompt/cache work with no anchoring epic clause or AC.
A reviewer tracing c403 up to its parent for the containing contract cannot locate any epic clause the leaf narrows.
findings.suggested_fix: Move c403 (and its siblings 8415/e3cd) under the overlap-judge epic that owns src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py (docstring: 'only-crave-art, story 9022'), whose plan already contains this subsystem; alternatively, if 061c is intended as the umbrella, add a scope clause + AC to 061c naming the overlap-judge cache-economics work so the leaf is contained.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a prior-art paragraph to Approach/Scope that names spec_scan.py's batch-evaluator, review_kernel.reshape_verifications (the deliberately-single demux/keying seam decide_ops.py routes through), and xcheck.py's permissive-fail-safe list contract, and either REUSE the shared reshape seam for overlap_verdict_batch's per-candidate demux (absent/unknown-label/malformed) or justify a bespoke implementation against Rule-of-Three.
evidence: Plan proposes fresh work: judge.py gains 'batch construction (a labelled candidate list, the batch-size bound) and per-candidate response demultiplexing'; a new overlap_verdict_batch contract; and demux tests where 'a candidate absent from the response, and a response entry naming an unknown label, both resolve to abstain'.

Prior art 1 — src/rebar/llm/spec_scan.py:3-5 is an explicit 'batch evaluator ... candidate epics are chunked into batches, each batch is evaluated against the spec in its own runner pass (bounded cost)'; spec_scan.py:106-128 chunks candidates and labels each by ticket id in one RunRequest per batch — the same labelled-list + batch-bound + chunking shape the plan proposes.

Prior art 2 — src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:186-236 defines reshape_verifications/VerificationReshape as 'the SINGLE place a flat verifier output list becomes the {index: verification} map', classifying malformed / duplicates / unexpected(out-of-range index) / missing(no-verification -> INDETERMINATE) — the exact demux + fail-safe (missing->abstain, unknown label->abstain, malformed->fail-safe) the plan proposes to build fresh in judge.py.
Prior art 2 is deliberately SHARED: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/decide_ops.py:186-193 routes through review_kernel.reshape_verifications precisely 'so this op no longer re-implements the silent-drop'.

Prior art 3 — src/rebar/llm/plan_review/xcheck.py:37-55 models a flat list of per-item judgments keyed by index with 'Fields ... permissive so ONE malformed item reshapes to the fail-safe KEEP rather than failing the whole structured batch' — the same fail-safe contract shape proposed for overlap_verdict_batch.

docs/reuse-surface.md:417-422 documents an established culture of centralizing reshape/demux seams (reshape_novelties/reshape_verifications) reused across gates — the reuse surface the plan does not evaluate against.

ABSENCE: the plan's prior-art reasoning is entirely on the token/caching axis (8415/afeb/e3cd/1024 floor); nothing in Approach or Scope names spec_scan, reshape_verifications, or the xcheck fail-safe contract, nor justifies a bespoke demux over the shared seam (Rule-of-Three: this would be the 3rd+ per-item demux).
findings.finding: The plan builds a batch-evaluator + per-item demultiplex/fail-safe seam in overlap/judge.py and contracts.py without considering three near-exact in-repo prior-art implementations, so it risks re-implementing (repackaging) an already-centralized pattern.
findings.location: Approach + Scope: src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py (per-candidate response demultiplexing), src/rebar/llm/contracts.py (new overlap_verdict_batch fail-safe contract), Testing (Demultiplexing / Fail-safe / Batch bound)
scenarios: A future edit to abstain-on-missing/unknown-label semantics must now be made in judge.py AND in reshape_verifications/xcheck, because the contract was duplicated rather than reused — the exact drift the shared seam exists to prevent.
A reviewer or the author cannot tell whether the bespoke demux is warranted (different enough) or accidental repackaging, because no comparison to the existing seams is on the record.

findings.checklist_item: State the default batch-size bound value (a concrete integer) in judge.py's constant, so the executor need not choose it.
evidence: Scope bullet names 'the batch-size bound' and 'a module constant in judge.py, since no operator-facing tuning is claimed for it' but gives no value
Examples use N=6 with 'one batch per ordering' implying bound >= 6, but the constant's value is undecided
Testing bullet 'a corpus larger than the bound is split into multiple calls' exercises the bound without pinning its value
findings.finding: The batch-size bound is named as a module constant but its actual value is never stated, leaving the executor to choose the number.
findings.location: Scope: 'the batch bound is a module constant in judge.py'
scenarios: Executor picks an arbitrary batch size; too large risks worse cross-contamination, too small forfeits the call-count savings
findings.suggested_fix: Name a concrete default (e.g. BATCH_SIZE = 8) in the Scope bullet, and note the precision-vs-savings tradeoff that justifies it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the title with the body: reword the headline so the committed outcome (fewer calls / net-positive input tokens) is what it promises, with floor-clearing framed as the measured bet the body already treats it as.
evidence: Title: 'Batch overlap-judge candidates so the shared prefix clears the 1024-token cache floor'
Body: 'whether base 423 + section + digest 306-453 clears 1024 for every real digest is an empirical question this ticket answers ... it may come out short'
AC: 'a prefix that still does not clear the floor is recorded as such rather than presented as a caching win'
findings.finding: The title promises the batching will 'clear the 1024-token cache floor', but the body explicitly frames floor-clearing as a bet that may fail ('A prefix that still does not cache is a valid recorded outcome; mechanism 1 carries the ticket in that case'), so the headline over-promises the outcome relative to what the plan commits to deliver.
findings.location: Title vs. Approach mechanism 2 / AC 'The prefix bet is reported either way'
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to lead with the arithmetic win, e.g. 'Batch overlap-judge candidates per call to cut call volume (and measure whether the grown prefix clears the 1024 cache floor)'.
